title: HoloMotion · SuperMimic
evidence:
- Integrates SuperMimic into HoloMotion’s G1 assets, HDF5 motion data and Hydra workflow, sharing tasks and evaluation with PPO on MuJoCo Warp and Isaac PhysX.
- Upstream report: The selected MuJoCo Warp recipe completes 32 / 40 LAFAN1 training clips after 30 minutes on one RTX 5090.
- Useful context: The validated route uses a compact policy. The preview shows short excerpts from a separate run; it does not replace complete-clip evaluation or establish the planned large-policy integration. Source snapshot.

title: supermimic_vibed
evidence:
- An independent G1 implementation on Isaac Lab 3, with a kit-less setup, training, full-clip evaluation and rendering tools.
- Upstream report: On 40 LAFAN1 clips, normalized return 0.829 and 0 / 40 failures after 1.47 hours on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
- Useful context: The author describes it as a rapid, unreviewed reproduction. Documented deviations include disabled self-collisions, bf16 MLP computation and an extra reference-root orientation input. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic-Reproduced
evidence:
- A from-scratch mjlab implementation for G1, with Chinese reproduction notes, LAFAN1/BONES-SEED processing, multi-GPU training, an interactive replay viewer and a released full-data checkpoint.
- Upstream report: With paper observations, four RTX 5090s train on 129,943 BONES-SEED clips for 7.1 hours (about 28 GPU·h). The experiment log reports 0.930 return, 495 / 129,943 failures on that library; after excluding 452 clips by name, it reports 0.932 return, 145 / 129,491 failures (0.11%) on the filtered evaluation set. On LAFAN1, anchor-relative observations reach 0.904, 3 / 40 failures, while paper observations reach 0.56–0.59, 3–9 / 40 across three runs.
- Useful context: BONES-SEED clips are short (median 5.8 seconds), whereas paper-observation policies drift on 100–300-second LAFAN1 clips. The two observation settings are not directly comparable. The upstream README pairs 0.930 with the filtered failure count; the set-specific figures above follow the experiment log. Source snapshot.

title: UniSuperMimic
evidence:
- Implements G1 tracking in UniLab with LAFAN1/BONES-SEED download, filtering, packing, training and full-clip evaluation, plus mjwarp, MuJoCo and Motrix entrypoints. The updated evaluator recycles finished environments to reduce long-clip batch tails.
- Upstream report: On 129,487 BONES-SEED clips, one RTX 4090 (48 GB as reported upstream) trains the 12k baseline in 1.69 h, with full-library return 0.9243 and 350 / 129,487 failures. Adding EMA, no-sync training and a learning-rate change on the same GPU reaches 0.9395 and 193 / 129,487 failures at 8k iterations. The older RTX 5090 / 10,000-clip sample is a separate run.
- Useful context: The explicitly paired 1.69 h belongs to the 12k baseline. The README also advertises a strong checkpoint in about 40 minutes, but does not give a precise elapsed time for the optimized 8k row. These are the reported mjwarp experiments, not equivalent validation across backends. BONES-SEED evaluation covers training motions, not held-out generalization. Source snapshot.

title: MorphMimic
evidence:
- Shares a world model, policy, or both across G1, X2 Ultra and T2 in mjlab / MuJoCo Warp. v0.1 adds a 24-joint / five-point human interface that consumes PICO body tracking directly, without first retargeting it to robot motion.
- Upstream report: Releases a unified 60,000-iteration ONNX policy for `g1_amber`, X2 Ultra and T2 with motion and human interfaces. The authors tested it on their real G1 and provide onboard teleoperation. X2 Ultra and T2 have only run in simulation; aggregate success rates and training duration are not reported.
- Useful context: The released `g1_amber` configuration adapts to the authors’ weak G1 waist motors; it is not validation on every G1. Later checkpoints from 78k onward swayed while standing on hardware despite apparently normal training metrics. Default interfaces do not need robot world pose; optional robot-anchor mode still needs pose estimation. Source snapshot.

title: InstantTrack
evidence:
- Builds on the mjlab port of supermimic_vibed for G1, combining GPU training-loop optimizations, EMA policy weights, a smaller world model and failure-focused resets; the main preset also adds a contact reward during imagined rollouts.
- Upstream report: On one RTX 5090, all three seeds reach return ≥ 0.82 and 0 / 40 failed LAFAN1 clips in about 15 minutes, with mean return 0.831 at that point. The reported 2.2× speed-up is against the author's SuperMimic + EMA baseline on the same machine; the 6× figure uses their plain reimplementation.
- Useful context: Time marks the first of three consecutive qualifying checkpoints, excludes offline evaluation and is not an end-to-end setup time. Evaluation covers the training clips in simulation; no larger motion library or real-robot results are reported. Model size, update count and training reward differ from the baseline; this is not a cross-project speed ranking. Source snapshot.

title: allmimic
evidence:
- Builds on supermimic_vibe for G1 in mjlab, mixing residual upper-body actions with absolute leg actions, weighting world-model losses and balancing motion sampling.
- Upstream report: With the recommended preset on one RTX 4090, full-length LAFAN1 evaluation reports 0 / 40 failures and return 0.91 after 0.83 hours; training time excludes evaluation.
- Useful context: The recommended preset changes the method and data sampling. The 306-hard-motion-only run and full BONES-SEED training are separate experiments. Source snapshot.

title: Rethinking SuperMimic
evidence:
- Studies goal conditioning for G1 in mjlab: concatenating the goal with proprioception versus using FiLM to modulate the policy layers. The latest revision adds an HL-Gauss critic, gradient checks and selectable heading- or pelvis-frame world-model coordinates.
- Useful context: Provides configurable observations, anchor choices and Viser playback. Its implementation table explains differences from the paper and supermimic_vibed, including self-collisions and observation inputs. Source snapshot.

title: Standing MBRL vs PPO
evidence:
- Adapts SuperMimic's differentiable world-model loop to a static G1 standing task and compares it with an RSL-RL PPO baseline derived from BeyondMimic.
- Upstream report: With the same 29-DoF G1, task, reward and about one hour of training on 256 environments, MBRL succeeds 32 / 32 times in both the 20-second and 60-second tests; PPO succeeds 12 / 32 and 16 / 32. Mean 20-second joint RMSE is 0.144 versus 0.415 rad.
- Useful context: Single training seed, shared GPU, no disturbances, and the 32 rollouts are copies rather than independent seeds. The project does not claim training-speed or real-robot gains. Source snapshot.

title: ScaleBFM_Plus · SuperMimic
evidence:
- Integrates SuperMimic-style world-model learning and 32-step BPTT into ScaleTrack for G1 in IsaacLab / RSL-RL, retaining the humanoid transformer and tracking modes, with PPO-compatible policy export and playback.
- Upstream report: Training on 309 h / 138k clips from BONES-SEED, any4hdmi and LAFAN1 for 8.3 h on 16 RTX 5090s yields 99.5% tracking success on 2,575 held-out motions. On 386 dynamic test motions, both this policy and the official ScaleBFM-M checkpoint succeed on 376 / 386, with mean global body-position errors of 6.35 cm and 6.43 cm, respectively.
- Useful context: This is a community extension of ScaleBFM. The reported 26× per-step speedup compares 0.65 s on 16 RTX 5090s with PPO's 17.0 s on 8 RTX 5090s; it is not a matched-compute or time-to-quality comparison. Source snapshot.

title: TrackerLab SuperMimic
evidence:
- Provides a shared Isaac Lab / PhysX workflow for retargeting, training, full-clip evaluation and export across G1, Go2, A3, T1, Bumi and Pi+, plus Go2 task policies.
- Upstream report: Re-evaluation of the 32,000-iteration G1 parent checkpoint reports normalized return 0.8694663 and 0 / 40 LAFAN1 failures.
- Useful context: Results use PhysX, while supermimic_vibed uses MuJoCo Warp. Robot-specific motion libraries and training histories differ; held-out motion generalization remains unmeasured. A separate G1 MuJoCo-Warp entrypoint and motion-tail/normalizer fixes are now available. The Warp integration has CPU regression coverage but still needs target-GPU qualification; it does not inherit the historical PhysX score above. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic Mjlab
evidence:
- An independent SuperMimic reproduction for Unitree G1 in mjlab, with a complete performance-improvement ablation study, multi-motion and velocity training, OOD playback, video-to-motion export, full-clip evaluation and released policy/world-model checkpoints.
- Upstream report: On all 40 LAFAN motions, the selected checkpoint achieves 40 / 40 successful motions, 100% mean completion and 0.8528 normalized return in fixed-start, full-clip deterministic evaluation. Training for 15,000 iterations takes approximately 4 hours on one RTX A6000 48 GB, with 4,096 environments and FP32 networks.
- Useful context: Documents the full progression from Actor/Critic input normalization through a torso-frame motion orientation anchor, world-model normalization and a corrected cosine learning-rate schedule: mean normalized return 0.6016 → 0.8130 → 0.8504 → 0.8526 at 15,000 iterations over all 40 motions. The final rerun mean is distinct from the selected checkpoint score above. Updated documentation adds the RoboJuDo-Plus SuperMimic deployment route; the authors report 23DoF G1 hardware use, with velocity tracking still in development. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic on LocoMuJoCo
evidence:
- Ports the method to H1 with JAX and LocoMuJoCo, adding a full-state ODE world model and anti-saturation regularization alongside the MLP, residual-expert, action-sensitivity and trust-aware variants.
- Upstream report: With fixed 5,000-iteration checkpoints and 160 initial states, adding anti-saturation to the Euler ODE model reduces aggregate failures from 15 / 480 to 1 / 480 over three seeds. Seed 43 improves from 878.71 / 15 failures to 935.38 / 0 failures, while seed 42 becomes slightly worse, so this is not a uniform score increase.
- Useful context: The reward is LocoMuJoCo episode return, not the G1 normalized tracking score. Midpoint ODE acceleration runs are still in progress and are not included as completed results. Source snapshot.

title: supermimic_vibe
evidence:
- An independent G1 reproduction in mjlab / MuJoCo Warp, with claim-by-claim PPO-Sim/PPO-WM, critic, horizon, push-recovery, velocity-control, BONES-SEED scaling and SONIC comparisons.
- Upstream report: One RTX A6000 reaches LAFAN1 return 0.833 at 1.34 h; its best checkpoint scores 0.947 with 0 / 40 failures at 11.4 h. On 128,904 BONES-SEED clips, a modified configuration collecting without exploration noise in half the environments reaches 0.923 and 45 / 128,904 failures at 14.4 h. Times exclude evaluation.
- Useful context: The noise-free collection fraction is an addition to the paper. The paper-faithful BONES-SEED run collapses after roughly six hours, and the two-GPU zero-failure result was not reproduced; these negative results are documented alongside ablations. A6000 and paper H100 timings are not equivalent; hardware transfer is out of scope. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimicKit
evidence:
- An independent MuJoCo Warp implementation for G1, H2 and A3, with motion retargeting, policy/world-model ONNX export and WebGPU browser previews.
- Upstream report: Publishes separate train40 and held-out val37 evaluations for G1/H2. The G1 55.5k preview reports 0.7990, 3 / 40 failures on train40 and 0.3103, 31 / 37 failures on val37; A3 100k full-clip evaluation is pending.
- Useful context: An experimental preview with limited held-out tracking and documented later-checkpoint regressions. Supply licensed motion data; no top-level code license was found at the reviewed revision. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic Lab
evidence:
- Packages a reusable SuperMimic learner and runner for Isaac Lab custom tasks, with a separately installable AGIBOT A3 example.
- What it provides: Provides task contracts, setup instructions and backend validation records. A custom task must supply differentiable state, observation, reward and termination functions.
- Useful context: Targets the Isaac Lab 3 development API. The A3 preview uses separately initialized segments; convergence, backend equivalence and hardware deployment are not established. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic on RTX 5080
evidence:
- An independent mjlab reproduction derived from CuboiLeo, configured for one 16 GB RTX 5080 with 2,048 training environments and additional anchor-relative observations.
- Upstream report: The 40k checkpoint reaches 0.8515 mean / 0.8608 step-weighted return with 2 / 40 failures after 2.7 hours. The 48k checkpoint averages 0.8375, 4–6 / 40 failures, after 3.3 hours over three evaluations.
- Useful context: This is a single training seed, and the extra anchor observations make it non-equivalent to the paper-observation protocol. The author highlights 40k as the preferred checkpoint but notes that 40k/44k/48k differences still require multiple seeds. Source snapshot.

title: InstinctMJ · SuperMimic
evidence:
- Implements perceptive G1 terrain tracking in mjlab / instinct_rl with two routes: Render ray-casts depth from predicted robot state; Latent predicts the depth encoder's features. Both feed stop-gradient encoder features to the actor; the encoder learns from reconstruction, with an annealed value head in Render.
- Upstream report: One RTX 3090, 1,024 training environments and 8,000 iterations, on 10 motions: Render 94.9% success, Latent 96.9%. Render takes about 2.7 h, evaluated with 3 seeds × 256 environments; the report has one training seed, and Latent uses 128 evaluation environments from the original pre-merge run.
- Useful context: Use the supermimic branch. Render without the value head reaches 91.0%; the removed policy-gradient-only encoder variant degraded below a random encoder. The two results have different evaluation setups. Rendering uses known scene meshes, not unknown real environments. Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. Source snapshot.

title: Go2-SuperMimic
evidence:
- Adapts SuperMimic to Unitree Go2 chase-and-dodge tasks in mjlab, covering flat ground, obstacles and terrain with LiDAR or height-scan inputs.
- What it provides: Publishes separate flat, obstacle and terrain actors, plus evaluation and recording tools. Actor-only downloads support playback; resuming training also needs the world model and critic.
- Useful context: Simulation only, with ground-truth target perception. The released terrain policy still has falls and bar collisions under the hardest settings. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic Parkour
evidence:
- A five-skill G1 parkour adaptation built on mjlab and PHP Parkour motion-matching data, using a shared differentiable world model and BPTT policy learning.
- Upstream report: Trains a policy to clear a 130 cm obstacle in just over 4 hours on one GPU, ships the resulting checkpoint and provides browser-based playback.
- Useful context: The PHP motion bundles are not distributed with the repository and must be supplied separately. This is one upstream demonstration and training-time claim, not an independent benchmark against PPO or SuperMimic. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic-perceptive
evidence:
- Builds on supermimic_vibed in Isaac Lab 3, pretraining a heightmap autoencoder and freezing one shared encoder for the actor, critic and world model.
- What it provides: Documents four flat-ground/step-terrain control experiments and separate reconstruction checks; the published control comparisons remain in progress.
- Useful context: Maps come from simulator ground truth. Real-depth reconstruction and hardware perception are not integrated, and inherited baseline scores do not establish gains from the encoder. Source snapshot.

title: Dex SuperMimic
evidence:
- Adapts world-model-based policy training to Wuji Hand 1/Hand 2 cube reorientation and Wuji Hand 2 pen spinning, using mjlab / MuJoCo Warp and the InstinctMJ task framework.
- What it provides: Three task configurations, bundled hand and cube assets, Viser playback, and three 8,000-iteration checkpoints in the `pretrained-wuji-v2` release.
- Useful context: This is a dexterous-manipulation adaptation with a different task and reward from humanoid motion tracking. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic for Robot Manipulation
evidence:
- Adapts SuperMimic to state-based manipulation with a simulated ARX5 arm in mjlab / MuJoCo Warp across the Lemon, BoxInBin and MugHang tasks.
- Upstream report: Held-out reset banks with 256 complete episodes per task at 4,000 iterations reach 100.0% Lemon, 94.9% BoxInBin and 96.9% MugHang success; the runs take 1.8 / 1.9 / 2.8 hours on one A100 80 GB while sharing the GPU.
- Useful context: OmniReset-style reset categories shorten the effective horizon, and contact-based success tests use differentiable geometric surrogates during imagination. The policy observes low-dimensional state only; released checkpoints and reset banks are on Hugging Face. Source snapshot.

title: In-Hand Rotation mjlab
evidence:
- Applies SuperMimic-style world-model policy learning (an MLP world model refit online, backpropagation through imagined rollouts, a TD(λ) critic and weight averaging) to the LEAP Hand in mjlab / MuJoCo Warp, next to PPO baselines on the same environments: palm-up cube yaw, SO(3) cube reorientation (PPO only) and palm-down fingertip rotation of 22 objects, on a servo model identified on the real hand. Checkpoints for both methods are released.
- Upstream report: On cube yaw, the world-model policy reaches PPO's level (≈0.26 reward/s) after 25 minutes and 18M env steps, where PPO needs 6.5 hours and 262M, and ends at 0.292 vs 0.261. On palm-down fingertip rotation (64 rollouts per object, 60 s, randomized pad friction 0.25–1.2), a joints-only world-model policy reaches 933° rewarded yaw with 4.0% drops, against 675° / 10.4% for the deployed PPO student distilled from a teacher, and 944° / 2.1% for the privileged PPO teacher.
- Useful context: World-model results are in simulation; the real-robot videos (yaw and SO(3)) show PPO policies. Fingertip numbers use the repository's own evaluation (rotation reward capped at 0.3 rad/s; a drop is 30 mm of drift). Single runs per configuration; wall-clock times are on one RTX 4090. Source snapshot.

title: Humanoid Mimic · SuperMimic
evidence:
- Compares SuperMimic and PPO-Sim on shared G1 walking, squatting and box-lifting tasks in mjlab; the repository also contains a separate AMP-PPO stack.
- Upstream report: Box-lift success reaches 100% at 31 million environment steps, reported for two SuperMimic seeds with 64 randomized evaluation episodes; success means finishing within 10 cm of the reference box height.
- Useful context: Those SuperMimic scores used clean observations. The newer evaluation adds observation noise, and the published checkpoints have not been re-evaluated under that setting. Source snapshot.

title: Muscle SuperMimic
evidence:
- Extends SuperMimic to muscle-driven whole-body tracking on MS-Human-700 (700 muscles) and MyoFullBody (354 muscles) in mjlab / MuJoCo Warp.
- Upstream report: On MuscleMimic's 108 held-out KIT clips with 4,096 environments on one RTX 5090, MS-Human-700 reaches 0.91 normalized return after 10.1 hours (iteration 16k, 104 / 108 tracked); MyoFullBody reaches 0.83 after 6.0 hours (iteration 10k, 101 / 108 tracked).
- Useful context: Active development. The policy controls muscle excitation at 100 Hz, and the project provides a differentiable torch muscle model plus retargeting tools. The retargeted KIT data is gated and subject to AMASS terms; MS-Human-700 is provided as a Git submodule. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic Backflip Diagnostics
evidence:
- A focused G1 backflip study on Isaac Lab 3 and one RTX 5090, tracking leg symmetry, contact forces, penetration and landing stability.
- Upstream report: The final V14 checkpoint completes the rotation and landing hold, but the original strict evaluation records one frame of non-foot penetration and fails acceptance.
- Useful context: An independent rerun changes the borderline contact outcome. Both records are retained, so the clip should not be read as robust success or reproduction of all paper experiments. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic-PERA
evidence:
- Builds on UniSuperMimic for G1 interaction experiments, retaining a frozen tracker while developing separate interaction policies in UniLab / MuJoCo.
- Upstream report: A separate skateboarding policy completes 30-second simulated runs from one standard and eight held-out perturbed initial states, traveling 39.87–42.13 m.
- Useful context: Tracking and skateboarding are selected as separate branches. A shared world-model-driven interaction actor is not established; box handling and stairs remain unsuccessful in the reported prototype. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic-MuJoCo
evidence:
- A standalone mjlab / CPU MuJoCo port of supermimic_vibed for G1, with observation-compatibility profiles, inference weights and held-out 100STYLE evaluation.
- Upstream report: The fixed 98k policy completes 40 / 40 LAFAN training motions at return 0.8713, and 3,569 / 3,573 unseen 100STYLE clips at 0.8045, without fine-tuning.
- Useful context: Mean clip duration is 18.77 s for 100STYLE versus 220.55 s for LAFAN; retargeting also differs. Completion only means no termination, not accurate tracking. Cross-source semantic duplicates were not checked. The inference checkpoint does not resume full training. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic Retargeted
evidence:
- Extends the CuboiLeo mjlab baseline to G1, A3 and X2 Ultra, adding robot-specific kinematics, SOMA retargeting, coordinate corrections and foot-contact checks.
- What it provides: Publishes LAFAN1/BONES-SEED preparation workflows and historical evaluation records. Training weights are not distributed, and motion data must be prepared separately.
- Useful context: The reported policies use extra anchor-relative observations computed from simulator truth. These require corresponding state estimation on hardware; real-robot transfer is not validated. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic Wheel-Legged (wheelbipe)
evidence:
- Downstream port of SuperMimic to the wheeled-legged wheelbipe V14_2. The humanoid motion library is replaced by a velocity-command library; a 6-DoF action policy (four leg targets plus two wheel speeds) is optimised inside the differentiable world model, with PhysX / Isaac Lab as the data source and no PPO in the loop.
- Upstream report: On a 16-command grid the unified checkpoint reaches 0 / 16 falls and normalized return 0.983; a speed-focused checkpoint tracks 1.40 m/s at 0.01 error, and yaw reaches 10.21 rad/s (1.62 rev/s) with a 0.20-0.28 m leg cycle. Single RTX 4090, 4096 environments, 3.72 h cumulative over resumed runs; one run, no seed sweep.
- Useful context: A pretrained PPO policy for the same robot is mixed into the world-model buffer for the first 800 iterations only, and no teacher-free ablation was run, so these numbers are not attributable to the method alone. The port requires the robot USD asset from the upstream repository; there is no URDF. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic E1
evidence:
- Adapts the Isaac Lab 3 implementation to the 21-DoF DroidUp E1, with standalone native-MuJoCo sim-to-sim playback and evaluation.
- Upstream report: The 164k checkpoint completes 40 / 40 training motions, return 0.8559, in Isaac Lab. A separate 168k checkpoint completes 10 / 10 sampled eight-second segments in native MuJoCo.
- Useful context: Complete-clip evaluation and independently initialized short segments use different protocols. Neither result measures unseen-motion generalization or hardware transfer. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic Oli
evidence:
- Ports supermimic_vibed to the 31-DoF LimX Oli in Isaac Lab 3, adding motion retargeting, robot kinematics and full-motion video export.
- Upstream report: At iteration 18,000, the original 40-motion LAFAN1 evaluation reports return 0.6783 and 36 / 40 completed clips, after about 2.20 hours on one RTX 4090.
- Useful context: The displayed walking clip is a selected excerpt. Use the full-library evaluation when judging tracking coverage. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic on Apple M5
evidence:
- Adapts the CuboiLeo G1 baseline to Apple Silicon, using CPU MuJoCo for physics and PyTorch MPS for learning, with released weights and playback tools.
- Upstream report: For the released 21k checkpoint on a 24 GB Apple M5, seed 0, the original 40-motion evaluation reports return 0.7081 and 25 / 40 completed clips; a fresh-environment check completes 26 / 40.
- Useful context: Return is normalized by executed steps without zero-padding after failure, and the actor uses nine extra anchor-observation dimensions. Read return together with completion; held-out generalization is untested. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic-Repro-Sim2Real
evidence:
- Extends the CuboiLeo mjlab baseline with custom dance/video-motion tools, clip-specific fine-tuning, ONNX export and G1 deployment through native MuJoCo and the Unitree SDK.
- Upstream report: v1.0 publishes a roughly 46-second real-G1 dance assembled from four motion segments. In v1.1, the clip-specific `e24_0355000` policy completed a roughly 22-second dance twice on the real G1, including two rapid turns and a one-foot landing jump; nine earlier models had failed this clip. Both v1.1 runs used a slack safety tether, and repeating one model is not an ablation.
- Useful context: The v1.1 checkpoint is specialized to that single dance, not general motion tracking. Paper-style observations and anchor-augmented training remain separate configurations. Source snapshot.

title: SuperMimic G1 Deployment
evidence:
- A deployment runtime for a SuperMimic-Reproduced policy on the 29-DoF G1, using ONNX Runtime, MuJoCo and Unitree SDK2.
- What it provides: Provides both simulation and real-G1 demos, with separate guides for fetching deployment assets and running the policy on each target.
- Useful context: This repository covers deployment, not a new training benchmark. Motion data, model weights and robot assets retain their own terms beyond the code license. Source snapshot.

title: FlatWorld · SuperMimic-2D
evidence:
- Recreates the shared-world-model and imagined-policy-learning loop in FlatWorld with an eight-joint 2D humanoid and motion-tracking tasks.
- What it provides: Provides training, reference baking, per-skill rendering and a 33.3-second multi-skill promo covering walking, running, jumping, dancing, fighting, crouching and fall/get-up.
- Useful context: References are procedural, LAFAN-like 2D motions, not the LAFAN1 dataset. The character also uses a mild root assist, so this is an illustrative adaptation rather than a G1 benchmark. Source snapshot.

title: G0.5 · SuperMimic-style Steering
evidence:
- Transfers SuperMimic-style gradient-based learning to G0.5 VLA steering on LIBERO: a noise policy is trained through a frozen flow sampler using world-model and critic gradients.
- Useful context: This is one task-specific steering experiment within a broader VLA stack. The linked script identifies the relevant method; the repository’s other planning and memory results are separate experiments. Source snapshot.
